selected_news.source_headline: Azerbaijan welcomes Sinirlioglu’s candidacy for UN secretary-general
selected_news.article_text: Azerbaijan has welcomed the candidacy of Feridun Sinirlioglu, secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), for the top post at the United Nations. Azerbaijani Foreign Ministry spokesperson Ayhan Hacizade said so in a written statement on the selection of the next U.N. secretary-general. He said Baku “welcomes” Sinirlioglu’s nomination. Hacizade said the choice should rest on candidates’ professional qualifications, diplomatic experience and impartiality. He added that a candidate also needs the ability to build consensus among member states. He stressed that the selection process should be conducted in line with the U.N. Charter. Hacizade said Azerbaijan believes ongoing consultations and constructive dialogue among member states will produce an appropriate decision. In his words, that outcome would strengthen the U.N.’s capacity to respond more effectively to today’s global challenges. Sinirlioglu, a career Turkish diplomat, was elected OSCE secretary-general in December 2024 at the organization’s ministerial council meeting in Malta. He is the first Turkish citizen to hold that post. He previously served as Türkiye’s ambassador to the United Nations. Reports earlier in October said Türkiye was weighing whether to put him forward, and that he had discussed a possible bid on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. At the time, Türkiye had not formally nominated him. Under the U.N. process, the 15-member Security Council selects a candidate, and each of its five permanent members holds a veto. The 193-member General Assembly then gives final approval. The next secretary-general is due to take office on Jan. 1, 2027

selected_news.title: Trump, Iowa mitinginde El‑Sayed’i “cihadist” diye suçladı
selected_news.summary: President again took aim at progressive Senate candidate and lauded Haley Stevens for endorsing Mike Rogers Donald Trump railed against Democratic US senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign event in Iowa Sunday, repeatedly referring to the Michigan progressive as a “jihadist”. Trump’s comments aimed to influence a neck-and-neck race that will play an outsized role in determining which party controls the senate after Tuesday’s midterm elections. Continue reading...
selected_news.source_headline: Trump launches racist diatribe against Abdul El-Sayed at Iowa rally
selected_news.article_text: President again took aim at progressive Senate candidate and lauded Haley Stevens for endorsing Mike Rogers Donald Trump railed against Democratic US senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed at a campaign event in Iowa Sunday, repeatedly referring to the Michigan progressive as a “jihadist” Trump’s comments aimed to influence a neck-and-neck race that will play an outsized role in determining which party controls the senate after Tuesday’s midterm elections The president bashed El-Sayed, a practicing Muslim, in brazenly racist terms, saying that Congress would have to “get a special metal detector for Abdul” if he were elected “If you vote for this jihadist lunatic that wants to destroy you, you’re crazy,” Trump said The Michigan race has drawn national attention in recent days, as Hayley Stevens, who lost to El-Sayed in the August primary election, declined to campaign with him, while demanding that he publicly disavow an outside group’s political ad that posited a link between rising prices and US military support for Israel’s war on Gaza El-Sayed responded by telling Stevens to stay away from a campaign event at which they were supposed to appear together on Sunday. Stevens turned around and endorsed Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s Republican opponent. Steven’s high-profile defection in the waning hours of the tight race drew the condemnation of Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, who is Jewish Trump, on the other hand, heaped praise on Stevens for turning against El-Sayed, urging her to join the GOP “It was an incredible thing,” Trump said. “I’d love her to join the Republican party. I think that could happen.” Trump then lauded Rogers in metaphorical terms “Mike Rodgers is apple pie,” Trump said. “And you know what this country needs? A little apple pie. We don’t need the communists or jihadists, the Muslim Brotherhood. We need apple pie. He’s apple pie. He’ll be good.” Trump had little time to watch football this weekend, he noted, because he had been “going to these damn rallies all over the place” “Pretend I’m on the ballot,” Trump said. “Essentially, I am on the ballot.”

selected_news.title: Florida’da 12:50'de Learjet 60 çarpıştı, 9 ölü
selected_news.summary: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway. Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said. Continue reading...
selected_news.source_headline: All nine people aboard business jet that crashed in Florida have died
selected_news.article_text: Aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport and was headed to the Bahamas when it crashed All nine people have died who were aboard a business jet that crashed in a Florida neighborhood on Sunday, Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, said. The aircraft erupted in a massive fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway Duffy posted on X on Sunday that the Learjet 60 crashed in Palm Beach county at 12.50pm and called it a “horrific tragedy”. The Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the cause, he said The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom international airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for the airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight “This is definitely a tragedy,” he said He said the tail number for the flight was N722BD Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach county sheriff’s office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash The circumstances of the crash remained under investigation
